findings.title: Pillar 11 git-op pre-check fired on enforcement narration (false-positive shape)
findings.detail: v1 audit auto-injected an AUDIT-PILLAR11 critical finding because the deterministic regex `_GIT_OP_PATTERNS` in src/aho/council/audit.py:115-118 matched the strings 'git commit', 'git push', 'git merge', 'git add' inside the acceptance archive's own Pillar 11 invariant narration ("No `git commit`, `git push`, `git merge`, `git add`, `git rm`, secret read, or wrapper-bypass invocations from this session"). The regex didn't see the negation. Closure: added `_GIT_OP_ENFORCEMENT_SENTINELS` regex with ±150-char context window in src/aho/council/audit.py - sentinels capture canonical aho enforcement vocabulary (operator-only, operator-side, operator-action, operator-executed, agent surfaces, never executes, OPR-, 'no `git'). When any sentinel hits within window of a git-op match, the hit is suppressed. 13-test lock-in at artifacts/tests/test_audit_git_op_suppression.py covers: plain hits preserved (safety property), each canonical sentinel suppresses, the literal v1 false-positive shape suppresses, hits outside window still fire, gh pr patterns subject to same rule. v2 audit confirmed `git_ops_referenced: pass` (was `fail`).

findings.title: RAG enrichment status echo as findings (small-model false-positive shape #2)
findings.detail: v2 audit returned 2 findings whose descriptions were the literal RAG enrichment status template `{ID} ({kind}) - status: \`registered|unverified\`` with no substantive content. The model paraphrased the registered-references context section as findings - the auditor was supposed to *use* that section as ground truth, not echo it. The W4 deterministic post-hoc filter (audit_finding_filter.py) was structurally narrow to the F-0.2.17-W3-001 fake-ID-phrase shape and didn't catch this. Closure: added `_RAG_STATUS_ECHO_PATTERN` regex + `RAG_STATUS_ECHO_REASON` suppression branch in src/aho/council/audit_finding_filter.py. Tight whole-description anchor: any substantive sentence beyond the template defeats the match (safety property). Refactored `_filter_one` to accept `eligible_for_fake_id_rule` keyword so the new echo rule fires regardless of registered-set size (echo is description-shape-driven, not phrase-driven). 9 echo-suppression tests in artifacts/tests/test_audit_rag_echo_and_halt_downgrade.py cover registered + unverified echoes, em-dash + hyphen variants, with-substance preservation, two-echo full-suppression, fake-ID rule still fires alongside.

findings.title: Halt disposition uncoupled from filter outcome (orchestration gap)
findings.detail: Even after F-0.2.18-W0-006 filter extension, the model's raw `halt` disposition stood independent of filter results - if all model findings were filter-suppressed and no pre-check fired, the halt was materially unsupported but blocked workstream_complete. The existing structural override (audit.py:704-707) only handled the inverse case (model said `clean`, pre-checks failed → escalate to `surface_to_drafter`). Closure: added `unsupported_halt_downgrade` branch in src/aho/council/audit.py - when `final_disposition == 'halt'` AND `len(model_findings_active) == 0` AND `len(extra_findings) == 0`, downgrade to `surface_to_drafter`. NEVER `clean` - the model still emitted a halt signal, so drafter/operator arbitration is the right backstop. Added `unsupported_halt_downgrade: bool` to audit return dict + emitter document for downstream observability. 6 downgrade tests cover: only-echo-findings downgrades; substantive finding keeps halt; no-findings-at-all downgrades; pre-check-fail keeps halt; clean unaffected; surface_to_drafter unaffected. Also updated existing test_audit_finding_filter.py::test_audit_integration_suppresses_fake_id_finding to reflect the new contract (was asserting old 'disposition untouched' invariant).

findings.title: Narrative-lift residual: small-model semantic-discrimination limitation (operator-arbitrated)
findings.detail: v3 audit (run after F-0.2.18-W0-005/006/007 fixes landed) returned halt at confidence 0.90 with 2 model findings whose descriptions were verbatim quotes from the acceptance archive's own `audit_cycle_record` and `findings[F-0.2.18-W0-006]` narrative - text added in W0 to *document* the prior false-positive cycles. The model is lifting prior-cycle narrative as if it were a current finding. This is not a structural pattern (the descriptions don't match the RAG-echo template since they're prose, not ID-status echoes); it's a semantic-discrimination problem llama3.2:3b cannot solve at base tier. Three structural shapes are now closed (W0-005, W0-006, W0-007). The narrative-lift shape is operator-arbitrated per the F-0.2.17-W2-004 pattern. Possible future structural fix: verbatim-substring suppression filter (drop findings whose description is a ≥60-char substring of the audit target). Not landed in W0 because: (a) risks over-suppression on legitimate findings that quote the artifact, (b) a small-model can always be made to surface non-quote findings with different prose anchors so structural fixes have diminishing returns. Carry forward to 0.3.x or dedicated audit-machinery iteration.

operator_action_required.title: F-0.2.17-W1-003 - `ahomw:telegram_bot_token` rotation (pre-W2 hard gate)
operator_action_required.context: Carry-forward from 0.2.17 W1 D3 token-stdout exposure incident. Documented in iteration-close-0.2.17.md as hard gate before 0.3.1 (and by extension before 0.2.18 W2 since W2 lands install.fish on a new host).
operator_action_required.agent_recommendation: Operator rotates Telegram bot token before W2 launches. Operator action only (Pillar 11 - secrets). Agent does not execute.

actions_taken: Operator revoked the W1 D3-exposed token at @BotFather on Telegram. Old bytes no longer authenticate against api.telegram.org - the exposure risk that motivated F-0.2.17-W1-003 is materially closed.

Operator re-issued a new token and attempted store via `aho secret set ahomw telegram_bot_token`. First attempt and re-paste both stored a URL-shaped string (`https://api.telegram.org/bot<id>:<secret>`, 71 chars / 2 colons / sha256 prefixes `1c8b3e87` then `67c8fdb4`) instead of the bare token bytes. Telegram `getMe` returns `404 Not Found` against the stored value - the bridge daemon (`aho-telegram.service`) cannot authenticate until the stored value is the bare `<digits>:<35-char alphanum>` form.
resolution.operator_arbitration: The Telegram bridge being functional was never on the 0.2.18 graduation criterion (plan-doc §Graduation criterion steps 1–8 - install.fish + image + secrets broker + cross-host OTEL + materiality counter advance, no Telegram step). The hard-gate framing in 0.2.17 close-notes was specifically about the *exposure* of leaked bytes, not about restoring bridge functionality. With the old token revoked, the exposure risk is closed regardless of the malformed replacement. Operator arbitrates: bridge-restoration work is deferred as not-iteration-blocking; W0 closes on the security gate.
resolution.deferred_work: Bridge restoration (re-store bare-token bytes + restart `aho-telegram.service` + verify `getMe.ok==true`) carries forward outside the W0 framework. Not a 0.2.18 dependency.
